_note: Seed taxonomy of addictive design. Categories are grouped by mechanism, drawing on the two source taxonomies below. The full texts were not accessible when this was drafted, so the team should check category names and definitions against the papers before relying on them.

seed_sources.title: A taxonomy of technology design features that promote potentially addictive online behaviours
Defining, Classifying and Identifying Addictive Patterns in Digital Products
seed_sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Technology and Society, 2025

categories.name: Endless and frictionless consumption
categories.definition: Features that remove natural stopping points, so use continues without an active choice by the user.

categories.name: Variable and unpredictable rewards
categories.definition: Rewards delivered on an unpredictable schedule, which reinforces repeated checking or play.

categories.name: Social feedback and social pressure
categories.definition: Features that use approval, comparison or obligations to other people to bring users back.

categories.name: Notifications and re-engagement prompts
categories.definition: Prompts sent outside a session that pull the user back into the product.

categories.name: Streaks, goals and loss aversion
categories.definition: Progress mechanics that make stopping feel like losing something the user has already earned.

categories.name: Personalisation and immersion
categories.definition: Content selection and identity features that tailor the experience so it is harder to leave.

categories.name: Monetisation pressure
categories.definition: In app spending mechanics that hide the real cost or tie spending to the loops above.
